content:
Jess Rivera: Observed weirdly low KV reuse for multi-turn requests that share the same user prompt prefix. hit-rate graphs show spikes but overall reuse ~12% which is way lower than expected. Anyone seen client keys morphing between requests?
Sam Patel: Which part of the key are you normalizing? example of the key generation would help.
Jess Rivera: We log the key we send to runtime. Example: `tenant=redwood, model=redwood-3b, key=tenant:redwood|route:chat|session:abcd-1234|prefix:"What is the user's intent?"|ts:1700000000`
Jess Rivera: So `session` and `ts` get included by client SDK for tracing. Noticed different sessions per tab cause unique keys.
Anya Kozlova: Oof yeah that ts + ephemeral session id will kill reuse. :grimacing: We should separate "prefix identity" used for KV reuse from ephem metadata.
Kevin Wu: Agreed. Two options: 1) client SDK strips ephemeral fields when building cache key for prefix KV, or 2) have a canonicalization step server-side that maps incoming key -> reuse_bucket_key before lookup.
Marta Gomez: Did a quick sim where we canonicalized on the server by hashing only the prefix+model+tenant. Reuse jumped from 12% -> 68% for our sampled workload. Verified on bench-run.
Sam Patel: Nice. What's your canonicalization? share snippet.
Marta Gomez: ```python
# canonicalize prefix key
import hashlib

def canonical_prefix_key(tenant, model, prefix_text):
    h = hashlib.sha256(prefix_text.strip().lower().encode('utf-8')).hexdigest()[:16]
    return f\"kv:{tenant}:{model}:{h}\"
```
Sam Patel: That's exactly the idea. Trim/normalize whitespace, lowercasing, maybe collapse repeated punctuation. Also consider truncating long prefixes before hashing to avoid collisions?
Anya Kozlova: Don't truncate too aggressively — risk of collisions across distinct prompts. Use full hash but short hex slice ok for index. Add tenant+model salt to avoid cross-tenant collisions.
Jess Rivera: If we canonicalize server-side, we can still keep full original metadata for telemetry. So lookup uses canonical key but logs show original. Win-win.
Kevin Wu: Also watch for cache residency evictions. If we suddenly coalesce keys, hitset heat may change and push older entries out. We should simulate working set before rolling out.
Marta Gomez: Bench numbers: with canonical keys, median token latency stayed same, but cache hit ratio up -> 22% cost decrease in token compute in the sample. Memory pressure on KV nodes increased ~8% in short term (more shared hot entries). We then tightened LRU TTL from 48h->24h and saw stable memory.
Jess Rivera: Good to know. Any concerns about privacy? hashing prefixes could leak prompt content in telemetry if logs aren't protected.
Anya Kozlova: Use HMAC with tenant-specific secret for telemetry-safe keys if required. Or use blind-key pipeline: server derives lookup key using KMS-managed salt.
Sam Patel: Also found client SDK currently includes `route` and `session` in the top-level `cacheKey` when you call `client.chat()` — PR inbound to namespace ephemeral fields under `meta` only. That'll reduce accidental uniqueness.
infra-bot: benchmark-runner: bench/kv/coalesce-2024-10-03: canonicalization + client-fix improved reuse. full report: https://internal.redwood/bench/kv/coalesce-2024-10-03
Kevin Wu: For rollout plan: 1) ship client SDK change to stop injecting session/ts into prefix key (guarded by opt-in), 2) server-side canonicalization as fallback, 3) run A/B on small fraction of traffic, 4) monitor reuse, memory, and latencies.
Jess Rivera: @Sam can you open the client PR and link it here? I'll draft the server-side change and a bench harness for working-set sims.
Sam Patel: Yep, PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/725 - includes tests to ensure `meta` fields aren't folded into `cacheKey`.
Marta Gomez: I'll add a bench config that replays real prefix distribution and measure fragmentation/eviction over 72h.
Anya Kozlova: One more gotcha: some customers intentionally include tenant-level nonce in prompts (e.g., doc ids). We should document guidance: canonicalize only stable intent prefix slices (e.g., system prompt + user question), and provide opt-out for customers who want isolated cache per-session.
Jess Rivera: Great, let's proceed. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
